about.title: North Hollywood Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: North Hollywood sits at a crossroads of commuter traffic, Metro Red Line riders, and local residents navigating corridors like Lankershim Boulevard, Vineland Avenue, and the Ventura (101) and Hollywood (170) freeway interchanges. With Los Angeles County's dense traffic patterns running through the area, collisions happen at intersections, on-ramps, and in parking lots serving the arts district and nearby shopping centers. If you were hurt in one of these crashes, what happens in the days right after matters. Insurance adjusters often move quickly, sometimes asking for a recorded statement before you've even seen a doctor. LawProactive doesn't practice law ourselves; we're a free service that connects injured North Hollywood residents with an independent personal injury attorney who can evaluate the crash, help preserve evidence like traffic camera footage or vehicle data, and communicate with insurers on your behalf while you focus on recovering.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before Settling

items.title: California's Two-Year Clock
items.desc: California generally gives you two years from the crash date to file a car accident lawsuit, though claims involving a government vehicle or road hazard can require notice in as little as six months. An attorney can confirm which deadline applies to your situation early on.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Reduce, Not Bar, Recovery
items.desc: Under California's pure comparative fault rule, you can still recover damages even if you're partially at fault, though your share of responsibility reduces the amount. An independent attorney can help make sure the insurer isn't unfairly shifting blame onto you.

items.title: No Cap on Non-Economic Damages
items.desc: California places no statutory cap on compensation for pain, suffering, and other non-economic harm in most car accident cases. That makes it worth having someone experienced evaluate the full scope of what you've been through, not just the medical bills.

items.question: Should I give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurance company?
items.answer: It's generally best to avoid giving a recorded statement before speaking with an attorney, since anything you say can be used to minimize your claim later. Insurers may ask for one quickly, before you know the full extent of your injuries. An independent attorney connected through LawProactive can communicate with the insurer on your behalf instead.

items.question: What if my accident happened near the North Hollywood Metro station or involved a city vehicle?
items.answer: Claims involving a public transit vehicle or government-owned property, common near the Red Line station and surrounding streets, often carry a much shorter notice deadline than the standard two years. Missing that window can end your claim before it starts. It's worth having an attorney review the details as soon as possible.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge anything to connect me with an attorney?
items.answer: No, LawProactive's connection service is completely free to injured individuals. Attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning they only get paid if you recover compensation. There's no upfront cost or obligation to move forward.
